test_title: RRB NTPC CBT-I Official Paper (Held On: 12 Mar 2021 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: How many biodiversity hotspots does India host?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Four**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• India hosts** four biodiversity hotspots out of the 36** recognized worldwide.
 
• **The Himalayas**: Includes the entire Indian Himalayan region (and stretches into neighboring countries).
 
• **The Western Ghats**: Runs along the western coast of India and extends into the neighboring regions.
 
• **The Indo-Burma region**: Covers the northeastern parts of India and extends into Myanmar and parts of Southeast Asia.
 
• **The Sundaland**: Includes the Nicobar Islands, which are part of the larger Sundaland region that covers parts of Indonesia, Malaysia, and other areas.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **The Himalayas Geographic Range**: Spans five countries, including Bhutan, China, India, Nepal, and Pakistan. The Indian Himalayan region covers states like Jammu & Kashmir, Himachal Pradesh, Uttarakhand, Sikkim, Arunachal Pradesh, and the hill ranges of Assam and West Bengal.
 
• **The Western Ghats Geographic Range**: Runs along the western coast of India, extending from Gujarat to Kerala. It covers six states: Gujarat, Maharashtra, Goa, Karnataka, Tamil Nadu, and Kerala.
 
• **Indo-Burma Geographic Range**: Covers northeastern India, parts of Bangladesh, Myanmar, Thailand, Laos, Cambodia, and southern China.
 
• **Sundaland Geographic Range**: Primarily includes the Andaman and Nicobar Islands in India, and it stretches across Indonesia, Malaysia, Thailand, Brunei, and the Philippines.
 
• These regions host several critically endangered species, such as the **Asiatic lion, Ganges river dolphin, Western hoolock gibbon**, and numerous amphibians and reptiles.
